catalog_quote: [Table 3, Mansakan/other CPh speech varieties] 11. Davaweño (DavMk) Davao City (area) [native Mansakan dialect influenced by Tag and Ceb] (East. Mansakan) Wolff ... [sect. 2.3.2] Gallman (1974) treats several dialects of the Mansakan language community: Eastern Mansakan includes Mansaka, Mandayan, Boso, Caraga, and Kabasagan; Western Mansakan includes Kalagan, Tagakaolo, and Isamal. To these can be added: Kamayo (northern and southern dialects), Davaweño, and the distantly related Mamanwa language ... [sect. 3.1.3 Accent] The accentual systems of all other Bs dialects have phonetic details involving both vowel length and stress. ... [fn. 70, p.298] Outside of the Bs group an example can be found in Mansakan. Kamayo generally preserves the PCP accent patterns, while Mansaka and Kalagan only have relics of proto accent (see 8.10.1.). Influence from other languages probably enters the pict…

audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: every component of the stitched deciding quote is in the held Zorc 1977 text layer at the stated locators (Table 3 item 11, 2.3.2, 3.1.3, fn.70), verbatim modulo scanned letter-spacing; Zorc 1977 contains no accent statement for Davaweño, exactly as the record says, and the earlier screen/the earlier screen attribution of the Bisayan accent rule to Davaweño was a misreading that A/B already corrected. (2) The deciding source is a 1977 comparative-historical dissertation in which Davaweño is a comparison variety; but no dedicated description of Davawenyo phonology exists: Glottolog 5.1 lists one descriptive work (Lee 2004, clitic ordering), and an open-web sweep (Wikipedia/Mansakan refs, zorc.net Mansakan folder, ANU repository, SIL Philippines archive, Iglesia et al. 2024 archival survey) found only SIL wordlists (1971, 1973-74) and a 1973 text, Gallman 1979 (subgrouping only, fetched sources

sources.quote: Only: 'Davaoeño (Dabawenyo): A language of the Davao Region, influenced by Cebuano and Tagalog. – a Mansakan language in the Central Philippine subgroup'. Nothing on accent.

sources.citation: Iglesia, Jessa Jane, Sajed S. Ingilan & Saeed Al Qumairi. 2024. The development of Kalagan and Isamal linguistics: an archival research. Southeastern Philippines Journal of Research and Development 29(2): 191-. DOI 10.53899/spjrd.v29i2.429
sources.quote: No statement on Davawenyo stress; useful only as a bibliography: the only Davawenyo materials it records are SIL wordlists (1971 Piso/Banaybanay; 1973 Kalagan-Davaweño, 372 items) and a 1973 text, all filed by SIL under Kalagan [kqe]. The one phonology it describes with 'length and stress' is of Kaagan-Kalagan (Hagonoy), not Davawenyo.
sources.locator: pp.193-196 and reference list (SIL 1971, 1973 Kalagan-Davawenyo wordlists; Compania 1973 text)

sources.citation: Gallman, Andrew F. 1979. Proto-South-East Mindanao and its internal relationships. In Gallman et al. (eds), Papers in Philippine Linguistics No. 10, 1-52. Pacific Linguistics A-55. Canberra: ANU. DOI 10.15144/PL-A55.1
sources.quote: None. Davawenyo (DVD/DVM) is discussed only for subgrouping (lexicostatistics, PEM *h > h in DVD, *r > r in DVM, assignment with Kamayo to 'Central-East Mindanao'); the PSEM phonology reconstructed covers segments only, no accent/stress section.
sources.locator: sect. 1.2 (p.3) and sect. 3 'The relationship of Kamayo and Davawenyo to the SEM languages' (pp.17-19); abbreviations DVD Davawenyo-Digos, DVM Davawenyo-Monay

sources.citation: Zorc, R. David. n.d. [c.1971-1976].
